description: Get one load of a Foundry ontology with its newest jobs (the load that writes it, and extracts that add documents to it): their status, phase, progress, error and spend. documents counts what it made of its documents, in all and by document set: how many a model read, how many its version does not read (not_read_by_version: stored and searchable, nothing in the graph), their fact writes, the reviews they left (left_for_review: counted as each document was written, so not the number still open) and names matched to no one record (names_unresolved, which overlaps the reviews). A job's progress counts a document as done whether or not it was read, so report documents' counts, not progress, when you say what a load read. documents can be absent though the load holds documents: its description says when. With wait, waits up to 25 s while it runs; call again until it ends.

load_id.description: The load's id, as helix_foundry_get_ontology or a create_load action returned it.

wait.description: Wait up to 25 s while it is writing or one of its jobs is queued or running, then return it either way; call again until it ends.

workspace_id.description: Helix workspace identifier. May be empty when the caller has only one workspace (a service key always does).

name: helix_foundry_get_load

documents.description: What the load made of the documents it holds. Absent in three cases, which a caller can't tell apart from this result alone: the load holds no documents (its version was given no document sets, or they hold no text document or PDF); the caller reads the load through source grants, in whole or in part; or the load was made before Foundry recorded which documents a load holds. So absence does not say nothing was left unread: when the load's version has document_set_ids, say the counts are unavailable and count from helix_foundry_list_documents.

duplicate.description: Documents whose text repeats another document's.

facts_written.description: Fact writes by the documents: each document counts the facts it created and the stored facts it added its evidence to, so a fact two documents state counts twice. It is not the number of distinct facts in the graph.

left_for_review.description: Reviews the documents left when the load last wrote each one, of every kind: statements held back instead of written as facts (scored under the bar, unverified, conflicting or breaking a rule), names matched to no one record, property values held back or in conflict, statements that fit no link, and links the load did write that a person can undo. A held statement or value is not in the graph. This is not the number of open reviews: a review a person settles stays counted until the load writes the decision, which a later load does (and the current load, where Foundry applies an approval, a chosen value or a resolve to it at once); a held statement written then leaves this count for facts_written. A property value in conflict stays counted after a person chooses its value: every load lists the conflict, and the choice settles it. helix_foundry_list_review_decisions lists what was settled.

names_unresolved.description: Names in the documents the load matched to no one record: none matched, several did, or its identifiers disagree. A statement about one is held, not written. Nearly every such name also left a review, so this overlaps left_for_review: don't add the two.

not_read_by_version.description: Documents the load's version does not read: no extraction route names their set. They are stored and their text is searchable, and nothing from them is in the graph. A new version whose goal covers them reads them.

read.description: Documents a model read for the names and facts they hold.

read_by_version.description: Whether an extraction route of the load's version reads the set: what the version routes, not what came of it, which read says. False: its documents are stored and searchable, and none of them is read for facts.

values_written.description: Values written by the documents: property values each document stated that were written as evidence, counted by document as facts_written is, so a value two documents state counts twice. A value held back or in conflict is a review, not a value written.

waiting.description: Documents the load has not extracted yet.

unread.description: Documents the model failed to read: absent when it failed none. They are not in the graph (no names or facts of them), so a load with unread documents is not complete: say how many went unread and why. A ready or partial load with them reads as ready, N documents not read (reason). A load whose every document the model failed is failed, its load job's error saying so.

documents.description: How many documents went unread because the model failed them.

model_failure.description: How the model failed most of them: quota, rate_limited, unavailable, timeout, auth, permission, not_found, unsupported, context_too_long and so on; absent when it wasn't recorded.

reason.description: A few words for why: provider quota, provider account, provider busy, too long for the model, model declined, model error, or model failed.

reread_at.description: When Helix reads them again on its own (RFC 3339), for the current load whose provider's quota, account or business is to blame: retried 15 minutes after the job that left them, then doubling up to every 6 hours, for about a week. Absent when the next job into the load or a new load reads them.

title: Get a Foundry load
